text: dsh-plugin-update 是 DSH Web 插件，在插件详情页显示 profile 插件的版本检查结果。它查询 npm 或受支持的 Git 来源，展示当前与最新版本，并在有兼容更新时提供更新按钮。主机端通过 DSH pluginManager 卸载并重新安装插件。代码无需 API Key；manifest 标记本插件已弃用，并称新版 DSH 已内置更新检查。

dsh-plugin-update is a DSH Web plugin for checking installed plugin versions. It queries npm or supported Git sources, shows current and newest versions, and lets users update through DSH pluginManager. Its manifest marks it deprecated and notes that current DSH has built-in update checks.
想在 DSH 插件详情页看看已安装的插件有没有新版本。
I want to update an installed DSH plugin from its details page.
dsh-plugin-update 的功能「检查和更新插件」：在插件详情页查询已安装插件的 npm 或受支持 Git 版本，显示当前与最新版本；用户可刷新检查，并通过按钮调用 DSH pluginManager 更新。
dsh-plugin-update 使用前须知：版本检查会向 npm registry 或受支持的 Git 主机请求包版本清单。（见 index.js:260-288、index.js:335-350）

English | [中文](README.zh.md)
dsh-plugin-update README · dsh-plugin-update：A DeepSeek Harness bundle that answers "is there a newer version of my plugin?" and updates it in one click — from the plugin's own detail page.
dsh-plugin-update README · The problem it solves：That sequence is easy to get wrong by hand and easy to forget. This bundle performs it for you.

dsh-plugin-update README · What it adds：Nothing in the sidebar. It contributes to the Plugins page's detail view, so the controls sit next to the ones the page already draws:

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| Detail page head | **Check for updates** beside the bundle's own switch and uninstall |
| Beside the title | **New version 4.10.0**, when a newer one exists |
| Under the page content | Installed → newest, the source that answered, and the reason when a check fails or the newest version needs a newer DSH |

dsh-plugin-update README · What it adds：- **npm** — the registry document's `latest` tag, through the same registries the profile's plugin manager uses, in the same order. A profile behind `registry.npmmirror.com` is checked against the mirror rather than npmjs.
- **Git** — the `version` in the repository's `package.json`, read from the default branch. `github:`, `gitlab:`, `bitbucket:`, `git+https://`, and `git@host:owner/repo` all resolve. A Git dependency names a branch rather than a version, so an update reinstalls the same spec and lets the branch supply the new code.

dsh-plugin-update README · What it adds：A local link, a tarball, or an alias has no remote to compare against, so the page says so instead of offering a button that cannot work. A Git address on a host with no readable raw file (a self-hosted server) is reported the same way.

Each bundle's check falls into five states:

dsh-plugin-update README · What it adds：- **update** — a newer version exists and `engines.dsh` (else the `@deepseek-ai/dsh` peer range) admits the running DSH version.
- **incompatible** — a newer version exists but requires a DSH this profile does not run. The requirement and its source are shown; no update button appears.
- **current** — the installed version is the newest one.
- **error** — the remote could not be read (offline, 404, a malformed document). The reason is shown, and **Check for updates** retries.
- **unsupported** — the dependency is a local link, a tarball, an alias, or a Git host this bundle cannot read. These are never touched.
dsh-plugin-update README · What it adds：Checking one page asks only that package: the other sources come from a ten-minute cache.

dsh-plugin-update README · How an update runs：The Host half calls the profile's own `pluginManager` service, exactly as the Plugins page and the `plugin_manager` tool do:

1. `removeBundle(name)` — deselects the bundle, unloads its rows, and runs `pnpm remove`.
2. `installBundle(spec, { enabled, registry })` — installs the new version and reselects the bundle. `enabled` preserves a bundle the person had switched off.
3. If step 2 fails, the previous spec is installed again, so a failed update does not leave the plugin missing.

dsh-plugin-update README · How an update runs：The saved spec keeps the range operator the dependency already used: `^4.8.1` becomes `^4.10.0`, not `4.10.0`. A profile that pinned an exact version stays pinned. A Git dependency keeps its Git address, since a version pin would freeze the branch.

dsh-plugin-update README · How an update runs：A Git update re-clones the repository, so it checks the host is reachable **before** removing anything. The plugin manager runs `git` with the environment it inherited and adds no proxy of its own; if the host is only reachable through a proxy that `git` does not see, the install would fail after the removal had already happened. The check uses the same no-proxy conditions, so such a host is refused while the plugin stays installed.

dsh-plugin-update README · How an update runs：With HMR enabled, the replacement applies without a restart; a bundle that was running since startup reports `restart-required`, and the page says so.

The bundle refuses to update itself: removing it would unload the routes answering the request.

Two side effects come from the plugin manager, not from this bundle, and they are the same ones the shipped Update performs:

dsh-plugin-update README · How an update runs：- The reinstalled bundle joins the **end** of `dsh.profile.bundles`. That order is configuration precedence, so a profile where two bundles override the same row sees the updated one win afterwards.
- A failed or cancelled installation after the removal leaves the package uninstalled; that is why the previous spec is installed again on failure, and why a Git host is proved reachable first.

dsh-plugin-update README · Configuration：None. The plugin manager's own `registry` and `fallbackRegistries` decide which registries are asked. Git manifests are read over HTTPS; when `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` is set, or the Windows per-user proxy is configured, that proxy is used for those reads.

dsh-plugin-update README · HTTP surface：Mutations require the `x-plugin-update: 1` header, which a cross-site form cannot set and a cross-origin `fetch` cannot send without a CORS preflight these exact routes never answer.

dsh-plugin-update README · Install：> **Deprecated:** do not install this plugin for new setups — upgrade to the
> latest DeepSeek Harness release and use its built-in update feature instead.
> The commands below are kept only for historical reference.

Straight from GitHub, which needs no download first:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> install https://github.com/YiZhiQvQ/dsh-plugin-update
```

A local checkout, which tracks edits in place:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> install /absolute/path/to/dsh-plugin-update
```

dsh-plugin-update README · Install：From the [Releases](https://github.com/YiZhiQvQ/dsh-plugin-update/releases) page:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> install /absolute/path/to/dsh-plugin-update-0.1.0.tgz
```

A tarball records a `file:` dependency pinned to that file's path, so keep the `.tgz` where it is or reinstall after moving it. A directory records a `link:` dependency. A GitHub install records the Git address, which `pnpm` can fetch again at any time.

dsh-plugin-update README · Tests：```sh
node --test test/helpers.test.js test/update.test.js
node test/dry-run.mjs
```

`update.test.js` serves canned registry documents through the global `fetch`, so its assertions do not move when a package is published. `dry-run.mjs` mounts the real `apply` on a fake context, serves the routes over a real HTTP socket, and prints the report it builds; set `globalThis.__DSH_BUNDLES__` and `globalThis.__DSH_REGISTRIES__` before importing it to feed it fixtures.
